reconcile.connective: Matthew Henry harmonizes the texts: 'came to his baptism' meant mere curiosity; only 'some' were actually baptized, the 'generality' refusing, per Luke.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain sense: Matthew depicts Pharisees coming to be baptized, which Luke explicitly says never happened.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/pharisees.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: It was strange that they came to John's baptism, but their curiosity brought them to be hearers; and some of them, it is probable, submitted to be baptized, but it is certain that the generality of them did not; for Christ says (Luk 7:29, Luk 7:30), that when the publicans justified God, and were baptized of John, the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Matthew Henry cross-references Luke 7:29-30 directly, explaining that only 'some' Pharisees were actually baptized while 'the generality' refused — reconciling Matthew's 'came to his baptism' with Luke's denial that they were baptized.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14), on Matthew 3:7
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Haley's Alleged Discrepancies was checked directly via full-text search and does not treat this specific passage; Matthew Henry's own note on Matthew 3:7 — already this row's reconcile-pole source — directly harmonizes Matthew's account with Luke 7:29-30.
